🎙 Iran’s VP says motorcycle licenses to women will be issued in coming weeks

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran is set to begin issuing motorcycle licenses to women in the coming weeks, the vice president for women and family affairs announces, stressing that there are no religious or legal restrictions preventing women from obtaining such licenses.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Zahra Behrouz Azar said women should have motorcycle licenses to avoid additional harm resulting from being unable to obtain insurance coverage due to not having a valid license.
​
She said the government had taken action on the issue with Parliament’s support, while religious scholars and clerics had also stated that issuing motorcycle licenses to women was not religiously prohibited.
​
Behrouz Azar said the necessary steps had been taken and that, according to her latest discussions with traffic police officials, a prototype motorcycle license for women had already been printed.
​
She said the issuance of the licenses had been delayed due to the outbreak of the recent US-Israeli war, adding that a ceremony to unveil the first motorcycle license for women had initially been planned for July.

🖥 International ‘Minab Lullabies of Awakening’ festival to be held in Iran

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The first International “Minab Lullabies of Awakening” Festival will be held with the participation of Iran’s Islamic Culture and Communications Organization, inviting mothers around the world to record lullabies for the children of Minab.

Festival secretary Maziar Rezakhani told IRNA on Tuesday that the event would be held in two sections, international and domestic, emphasizing that maternal love transcends geographical borders and lullabies are a shared language among mothers worldwide.
​
He said the festival aims to highlight the attack on Minab on the first day of the war launched by the US and Israel in early February, and counter attempts to obscure or distort the incident.
​
Rezakhani said the festival’s call for entries would be published soon, allowing artists from around the world to participate by creating and submitting works.
​
“At a time when the enemy is trying to conceal the full extent of the horrific crime at the Minab school, the need to hold such an artistic event has become more important than ever for artists, cultural and artistic officials, and freedom-loving people around the world,” he said.
​
At least 168 schoolchildren and their teachers were killed on February 28 when a US strike hit Shajareh-Tayyebeh primary school in Iran’s southern city of Minab.

🇷🇺📄The State Duma has passed a law prohibiting migrants with any criminal record from obtaining Russian citizenship or the right to reside in Russia.

According to current regulations, foreigners are denied citizenship if they have a criminal record for intentional crimes. Temporary and permanent residence permits are not issued to individuals with convictions for serious or particularly serious crimes. The law stipulates that citizenship, temporary residence permits, and permanent residence permits will not be granted to individuals with any outstanding or unpardoned criminal convictions. If documents have already been issued, they will be revoked upon discovery of an active conviction.

However, the document also states that these new regulations will not apply to foreigners who have been recognized as refugees or granted political asylum in Russia.

The law also introduces new requirements for applying for temporary and permanent residence permits. Specifically, migrants will be required to provide a paper document that either confirms the absence of a criminal record or contains information about the crimes for which the applicant has been convicted. This document must be issued by the competent authorities of the country where the migrant resides, no earlier than three months before the application is submitted. If a foreigner has multiple citizenships or several residence permits, they must provide the corresponding number of documents confirming the absence or presence of a criminal record.

It is stipulated that this document will not be required for foreigners under the age of 14, refugees who have been granted political asylum in Russia, and foreign citizens who have served or are currently serving in the Russian Armed Forces under contract.

🔻 Iran’s Army continues drone strikes on US bases in region

📌 Tehran, IRNA — The Army of the Islamic Republic of Iran has announced that its one-way attack drones targeted the Sheikh Isa base of the terrorist American army in Bahrain.

In its 20th phase of Operation Thunder and in multiple waves, the Army of the Islamic Republic of Iran struck the housing and staging areas of US terrorist forces at the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain with Arash one-way attack drones, the Army said in a statement on Tuesday.
​
The Sheikh Isa base is one of the most critical facilities of the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet and serves as the operational hub for the aggressive US military, from which air operations and drone control are directed.
​
Offensive operations will continue with full force until the enemy is stopped from further aggression against the country.

⚡️ Ex-Bolivian FM warns Trump’s actions—war, sanctions, assassinations—threaten global stability

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Former Bolivian Foreign Minister Fernando Huanacuni has strongly criticized US President Donald Trump’s policies, saying his “America First” approach has heightened tensions in the international order and that his policies have contributed to global instability.

In an exclusive interview with IRNA, Huanacuni said Trump’s policies toward Iran, Venezuela, Cuba, and Bolivia had weakened multilateral institutions, intensified economic pressure, and undermined countries’ national sovereignty.
​
“Trump’s policies are part of the United States’ broader effort to maintain its hegemony over other countries. However, what sets him apart from previous US administrations is the way he has openly and directly pursued this aggressive approach through unilateralism and coercive diplomacy,” the former minister said.
​
He added that Trump’s “America First” approach “has created tensions in the international order, while the US withdrawal or threats to withdraw from international agreements and institutions—including the Paris Agreement and the Iran nuclear deal—as well as its questioning of NATO, have weakened traditional alliances and mechanisms of global governance.”
​
“Undoubtedly, Trump poses a threat not only to the global order but also to humanity,” he added.
​
The former Bolivian minister criticized Washington’s policies toward Iran, saying severe economic sanctions had sought to cripple the Iranian economy and force Tehran into negotiations under tougher conditions.
​
The US war of aggression on Iran reflects Washington’s hostile policy and desire to control strategic resources, Huanacuni said, arguing that the US has long portrayed Latin Americans as “drug traffickers” and Middle Easterners as “terrorists” to justify assassinations and violations of international agreements.
​
Regarding Latin America, Huanacuni said US sanctions and economic pressure against Venezuela and Cuba had hindered their development and undermined their right to determine their own future.
​
On Bolivia, he said the US has historically sought to control Bolivia’s policies because of its abundant natural resources. However, Bolivia began reclaiming its national sovereignty in 2006, achieving significant economic progress and reducing dependence on conditional foreign aid, he added. He also said Bolivia must free itself from US interference and strengthen its historical and cultural awareness to unite its people and pursue development while preserving its sovereignty and national dignity.
